title: Toggle Categories and Labels in GMail
description: A quick tour of the Chrome extension: one click hides the GMail categories and labels you've already read.
meta: dblock/gmail-toggle · master @ bd6171a · screens from the project's demo recording · narration: ElevenLabs, voice Matilda · music: original

lexicon.github.com/dblock/gmail-toggle: github dot com slash d block slash Gmail toggle

scenes.title: A busy sidebar
steps: Got a lot of GMail labels? Here's what your sidebar looks like.
A long, long list, and you've already read almost all of it!

scenes.title: One button
steps: Meet the open envelope, right in the toolbar above your messages.
Hover for Toggle Read/Unread. Now click it!

scenes.title: Only what's unread
steps: Before the click, every single label.
After the click, only labels with unread mail, counts and all!
Their folders stay too, so you always know where a label lives.

scenes.title: Showing everything
steps: Click again, and everything's back. Nothing is moved or deleted.
And it remembers your choice the next time GMail loads!

scenes.title: Installing
steps: Want it? Find Toggle Categories and Labels in GMail in the Chrome Web Store, and click Add to Chrome.
Reload GMail, and the button is ready. Nothing to set up!

scenes.title: Get it
steps: It only runs on GMail, asks for no extra permissions, and never touches your mail.
It's free and open source, at github.com/dblock/gmail-toggle. Enjoy a tidier sidebar!
